What does the audit cover?
Your reputation today: Ratings, review volume, freshness, and other supported reputation measures.
Your competitive position: How your reputation compares with relevant local competitors.
Potential policy issues: Historic reviews and unusual competitor-review patterns that may warrant investigation.
Modeled improvement: Scenarios showing potential reputation changes, not promised results.

FAQs
Questions local businesses ask before getting started
Contact
How much work does setup take?
GatherUp is rated 9.2/10 for ease of setup on G2, and many businesses can get started in about an hour. Setup will involve confirming your business locations, designing your review request flow and adding your customer data.
Will GatherUp work with the tools I already use?
GatherUp works with most CRM and Point-of-Sales systems, some out of the box and others through an integration tool like Zapier. When you meet with the GatherUp team, they’ll be able to confirm the available connection, data requirements, and setup path you’ll need to launch.
Will AI respond to customers without my approval?
You control how automation fits into your workflow, including whether to use templates, AI-generated responses, or approval-based drafts. GatherUp can draft responses and handle routine replies automatically while preserving human oversight where brand voice, policy, compliance, or judgment matters.
Negative reviews are never answered automatically. A member of your team can review, edit, and approve the suggested response before it is posted.
What is Review Defense?
Review Defense is an automated protection layer that monitors your reviews for signs of suspicious activity or platform policy violations. It helps identify reviews that may be unfairly harming your reputation and, depending on your plan, supports or manages the dispute process on your behalf. It can also monitor competitors’ reviews to reveal suspicious activity that may be distorting how customers see the market.
How does Review Defense work?
Review Defense continuously analyzes new and existing reviews using evidence-based signals. When it identifies a review that may violate platform policy, it flags the review for your team and automatically submits a supported dispute, depending on your plan. It then tracks the dispute, records the outcome, and preserves the review history for your audit trail. The review platform makes the final removal decision.
Can GatherUp help with policy-violating reviews?
GatherUp helps identify, document, and dispute reviews showing signals of a policy violation. It also preserves a historical archive so you retain visibility after a review is removed from the public platform. No provider can responsibly guarantee removal or rating improvement.
Can I compare my reputation with competitors?
Yes. GatherUp supports comparison with up to 6 or 15 competitors depending on your tier. GatherUp surfaces review insights, opportunities, and gaps and can stack-rank performance using supported measures. The goal is to show where competitors have stronger reputation signals and what you can improve, not to reduce overall business quality to a single score.
Does GatherUp work for more than one location?
Yes. Central teams can standardize workflows, monitor performance, and report across locations while retaining the local detail needed to act.
What if an agency manages reputation for my business?
GatherUp serves both local businesses and agency partners. The GatherUp support team is available to answer any questions, however your agency team will be better able to answer specific questions about your service and the tools you’re using.

FAQs
The details people usually check before starting a trial or moving up a plan.
What happens during the 14-day trial?
Once you sign up, you get full access to GatherUp’s features so you can connect a customer list, send requests and see reviews arrive. No credit card is required to start, and nothing bills until you’re ready to continue.
How does multi-location pricing work?
Multiple Locations are priced per location, and the rate changes as your location count moves between tiers. Pick your range in the plan card, or talk to us for anything above ten locations.
Can I change or add locations later?
Yes. You can add locations at any time, and changing plans does not require starting over. If you are on an annual plan, whether billed upfront or monthly, you can add locations during your term but cannot remove them until the term ends. On a month-to-month plan, you can add or remove locations as needed. Billing adjusts from the effective date of each eligible change.
What counts as a location?
Each physical address or listing you manage counts as one location. Users are unlimited within a plan, so your whole team can work in the same account.
Are Listings Management and Review Defense included?
No, both are separate options that you can choose to add. Listings Management is priced per location, and Review Defense has its own three tiers.
Do you offer agency pricing?
Yes. Agency plans are quoted around your client portfolio and white-label needs, with pricing tiers set to work with your desired margin.
What billing options are available?
Reputation Management and Listings Management offer three options: month-to-month billing with no annual commitment, a discounted annual plan paid upfront, or a discounted annual plan paid in monthly installments. This lets you choose between flexibility and savings while spreading payments if needed.
Review Defense is available only with an annual commitment. You can pay for the year upfront at a discount or spread payments across the year in monthly installments. There is no month-to-month option.
Paying monthly is not always the same as a month-to-month plan. Annual plans require a full-year commitment, regardless of how you pay.
FAQs
What the tiers cover, how disputes work, and what we deliver.
Does Review Defense guarantee that fake reviews are removed?
No, and no provider can promise that responsibly. GatherUp identifies reviews showing signals of a policy violation, documents the evidence and submits supported disputes. The review platform makes the final removal decision.
How are disputes submitted?
On tiers that include disputes, supported cases are submitted automatically. You keep the evidence and history even after a review disappears from the public platform.
What does competitor coverage mean?
Competitor coverage is the number of local competitors you can monitor and compare with your business: up to six with Illuminate and 15 with Integrity. It helps you understand how your reputation compares, identify gaps and opportunities, and spot suspicious review patterns that may be creating an unfair advantage.
Integrity also includes automated, evidence-backed disputes against competitor reviews that appear to violate platform policy. The review platform makes the final decision on removal.
Do I need a Reputation Management plan to add Review Defense?
No. Review Defense is available on its own. You can choose the tier you’re interested in, including being able to choose different tiers if you have more than one business location.
What is the Transparency Certificate?
The Transparency Certificate is third-party verification that your reviews have passed an independent authenticity audit. It gives customers and AI tools a verifiable trust signal, helping your earned reputation stand out.
Certification is included free with every Review Defense plan (a $199-per-year value), subject to program eligibility and independent approval.
What is the difference between paying monthly and annually?
Both options are an annual commitment. Paying annually carries the lower per-month rate; paying monthly spreads the same commitment across twelve payments at a higher monthly figure.
What billing options are available?
Reputation Management and Listings Management offer three options: month-to-month billing with no annual commitment, a discounted annual plan paid upfront, or a discounted annual plan paid in monthly installments. This lets you choose between flexibility and savings while spreading payments if needed.
Review Defense is available only with an annual commitment. You can pay for the year upfront at a discount or spread payments across the year in monthly installments. There is no month-to-month option.
Paying monthly is not always the same as a month-to-month plan. Annual plans require a full-year commitment, regardless of how you pay.
FAQs
What to prepare before you sync, how quickly changes go live, and how coverage works.
Do I need Reputation Management or Review Defense first?
No. Listings Management is available as a standalone product, and you can also add it to Reputation Management or Review Defense. We find it’s a great complement to Reputation Management to cover both halves of how customers choose: accurate listings help them find you, and strong reviews help them pick you, all managed in one place.
What info do I need before syncing?
Business name, address, website, and primary category, all matching your Google Business Profile exactly to avoid reverification triggers.
What about service-area businesses?
Service-area businesses can enter an address, which is required to build listings, while choosing not to display it publicly. That gives full coverage without exposing a street address.
How fast do updates go live?
Updates sync immediately. Real-time connections publish your changes across directories automatically, so corrections are not left waiting on manual updates.
Why not just rely on Google?
Google gauges authority from a broader citation footprint, and Apple Maps, Bing, voice assistants, and AI tools all pull from other sources. Consistent listings across the wider network help each of them describe your business accurately.
How is Listings Management priced?
Listings Management is $40 per location per month. If you are adding 11 or more locations, contact us for volume pricing.

Built-in integrations
Start in minutes. No developer needed.
Universal Email Integration
Send review requests continuously using the transactional emails you already send. Each location gets its own email address: BCC it on receipts or thank-you emails, and GatherUp adds the customer and schedules a review request. It works with nearly any platform that sends email.
BCC and done
Add your location’s address to the BCC field of any transactional email template.
Automatic customer creation
Every BCC’d email adds the recipient as a customer, with no manual imports.
Flexible timing
Send immediately, or 1–23 hours, 1–7 days, or 1–12 weeks later, when customers are ready to share feedback.
Google Sheets
Connect a Google Sheet to any location, and every customer you add to it is imported automatically and sent a review request. GatherUp creates the spreadsheet for you, right in your Google Drive, in four quick setup steps.
Hourly sync
New rows are imported every hour, and each row’s status is written back to the sheet, so you can fix any errors in place.
Your send settings
Send by email, text, or both, immediately, at a scheduled daily time, or using your location’s existing settings.
Private by design
GatherUp only accesses spreadsheets the integration creates. The rest of your Drive stays private.
Connect thousands of apps with Zapier
If it connects to Zapier, it can send review requests through GatherUp.
Build workflows that send a review request when something happens in the tools you already use, and send new feedback back to them. No code required.
Explore GatherUp on Zapier ↗

Your Privacy Rights
Privacy Policy
Updated July 13th, 2026
On this page
This Privacy Policy describes our policies on the collection, use, and disclosure of information about you in connection with your use of our services, including those offered through our websites, emails, and mobile applications (collectively, the “Service”). The terms “we”, “us”, and “GatherUp” refer to GatherUp, LLC, doing business as GATHERUP in Walnut Creek, California. When you use the Service, you consent to our collection, use, and disclosure of information about you as described in this Privacy Policy.
1. INFORMATION WE COLLECT AND HOW WE USE IT
We may collect and store information about you when you use the Service. We use the information to fulfill your requests, provide the Service’s functionality, improve the Service’s quality, personalize your experience, track usage of the Service, provide feedback to third party businesses that are listed on the Service, market the Service, provide customer support, message you, back up our systems and allow for disaster recovery, enhance the security of the Service, and comply with legal obligations.
Among the information we collect, please note:
Account Information: If you create an account on GatherUp, we may store and use your name, email address and other information you may provide with your account. You can modify some of the information associated with your account by contacting us at support@gatherup.com.
Public Content: The information that you contribute through the Service is intended for public consumption, including your reviews, tips, photos, videos, check-ins, comments, likes, posts, bookmarks, friends, lists, compliments, and account profile. We may display this information through the Service, share it with businesses, and further distribute it to a wider audience through third party sites and services.
Activity: We may store information about your use of the Service, such as your search activity, the pages you view, the date and time of your visit, and reservations and purchases you make through the Service. We also may store information that your computer or mobile device provides to us in connection with your use of the Service, such as your browser type, type of computer or mobile device, browser language, IP address, mobile carrier, phone number, unique device identifier, advertising identifier, location (including geolocation, beacon based location, and GPS location), and requested and referring URLs. You may be able to disallow our use of certain location data through your device or browser settings, for example by disabling “Location Services” for the GatherUp application in iOS privacy settings.
2. Cookies
We, and third parties with whom we partner, may use cookies, web beacons, tags, scripts, local shared objects such as HTML5 and Flash (sometimes called “flash cookies”), advertising identifiers (including mobile identifiers such as Apple’s IDFA or Google’s Advertising ID) and similar technology (“Cookies”) in connection with your use of the Service, third party websites, and mobile applications. Cookies may have unique identifiers, and reside, among other places, on your computer or mobile device, in emails we send to you, and on our web pages. Cookies may transmit information about you and your use of the Service, such as your browser type, search preferences, IP address, and the date and time of your use. Cookies may be persistent or stored only during an individual session.
The purposes for which we use Cookies in the Service include:
Processes
Intended to make the Service work in the way you expect. For example, we use a Cookie that tells us whether you have already signed up for an account.
Authentication, Security, and Compliance
Intended to prevent fraud, protect your data from unauthorized parties, and comply with legal requirements. For example, we use Cookies to determine if you are logged in.
Preferences
Intended to remember information about how you prefer the Service to behave and look. For example, we use a Cookie that tells us whether you have declined to allow us to use your phone’s geolocation data.
Notifications
Intended to allow or prevent notices of information or options that we think could improve your use of the Service. For example, we use a Cookie that stops us from showing you the signup notification if you have already seen it.
Analytics
Intended to help us understand how visitors use the Service. For example, we use a Cookie that tells us how our search suggestions correlate to your interactions with the search page.
Managing Cookies: It may be possible to disable some (but not all) Cookies through your device or browser settings, but doing so may affect the functionality of the Service. The method for disabling Cookies may vary by device and browser, but can usually be found in preferences or security settings. For example, iOS and Android devices each have settings which are designed to limit forms of ad tracking. For flash cookies, you can manage your privacy settings by clicking here .
3. THIRD PARTIES
Third parties may receive information about you as follows:
Service Providers: We may rely on third party providers to support or provide some of the services that are available through the Service. We may also rely on third party providers to perform certain services for us in connection with your use of the Service, such as communications and hosting services, network security, technical and customer support, tracking and reporting functions, quality assurance testing, payment processing, our own marketing of the Service, and other functions. We may share information from or about you with these third party providers so that they can perform their services or complete your requests. These third party providers may share information with us that they obtain from or about you in connection with providing their services or completing your requests. Third party providers may also share this information with their subsidiaries, joint ventures, or other companies under common control. Some of our web pages utilize framing techniques to serve content to you from our third party providers, while preserving the look and feel of the Service. In such cases, please note that the information you provide is being provided to the third party.
Aggregate Information: We may share user information in the aggregate with third parties.
Business Transfers: We may share information from or about you with our parent companies, subsidiaries, joint ventures, or other companies under common control, in which case we will require them to honor this Privacy Policy. If another company acquires GatherUp or all or substantially all of our assets, that company will possess the same information, and will assume the rights and obligations with respect to that information as described in this Privacy Policy.
Businesses on GatherUp: We may share information from or about you (such as your age and gender), your submissions to the Service, your devices, and your use of the Service with businesses listed on GatherUp.
Investigations: We may investigate and disclose information from or about you if we have a good faith belief that such investigation or disclosure (a) is reasonably necessary to comply with legal process and law enforcement instructions and orders, such as a search warrant, subpoena, statute, judicial proceeding, or other legal process served on us; (b) is helpful to prevent, investigate, or identify possible wrongdoing in connection with the Service; or (c) protects our rights, reputation, property, or that of our users, affiliates, or the public. If you flag or otherwise complain to GatherUp about content through the Service, we may share the substance of your complaint with the contributor of that content in order to provide an opportunity for the contributor to respond.
Links: The Service may contain links to unaffiliated third party services. Except as set forth herein, we do not share your personal information with them, and are not responsible for their privacy practices. We suggest you read the privacy policies on or applicable to all such third party services.

4. DATA RETENTION AND ACCOUNT TERMINATION

If you become aware that a child has provided us with personal information without parental consent, please contact us here. If we become aware that a child under 13 has provided us with personal information without parental consent, we take steps to remove such information and terminate the child’s account.
6. SECURITY
We follow generally accepted industry standards to protect the personal information submitted to us, both during transmission and once we receive it. However, no method of transmission over the Internet or via mobile device, or method of electronic storage, is 100% secure. Therefore, while we strive to use commercially acceptable means to protect your personal information, we cannot guarantee its absolute security.
7. MODIFICATIONS TO THIS PRIVACY POLICY
We may revise this Privacy Policy from time to time. The most current version of the Privacy Policy will govern our collection, use, and disclosure of information about you and will be located here. 8. CALIFORNIA RESIDENTS: YOUR CALIFORNIA PRIVACY RIGHTS

9. GDPR COMPLIANCE
1) In effect from 25 May 2018, GatherUp will Process Personal Data in accordance with GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) requirements. https://www.eugdpr.org/
2) GatherUp is a “processor” by definition of the GDPR.
Definition: A processor is a natural or legal person or agency that processes data on behalf of a controller. “Processing” is defined very broadly in the Directive to include collection, use, storage, manipulation, disclosure, disposal, and virtually any other action with personal data.
GatherUp processes data as delegated by the “controller”.
Definition: A controller is as the natural or legal person or public agency that “alone or jointly with others” determines “the purposes and means of processing” personal data.
The GDPR defines the data controller as the principal party for responsibilities such as collecting consent, managing consent-revoking and enabling right to access. A data subject who wishes to revoke consent for his or her personal data therefore will contact the data controller to initiate the request.
3) Data Protection Impact Assessment. In effect from 25 May 2018, upon Customer’s request, GatherUp (processor) shall provide Customer with reasonable cooperation and assistance needed to fulfill Customer’s obligation under the GDPR to carry out a data protection impact assessment related to Customer’s use of the Services, to the extent Customer does not otherwise have access to the relevant information, and to the extent such information is available to GatherUp.
4) GatherUp shall return Customer Data to Customer and, to the extent allowed by applicable law, delete Customer Data in accordance with the procedures and timeframes specified by the GDPR.
5) Notification of Sub-processors and Objection Right for New Sub-processors. Customer acknowledges and expressly agrees that GatherUp does engage with Sub-processors and that GatherUp may engage in new Sub-processors at any time. All current Sub-processors have expressed their intention to be GDPR compliant by May 25th. List of current Sub-processors: SendGrid for Email delivery, Twilio for SMS delivery, Amazon AWS for data storage, Paypal Pro for payment processing, Campaign Monitor for Welcome and Marketing emails.
6) GatherUp maintains security incident management policies and procedures and shall notify Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to Customer Data, including Personal Data, transmitted, stored or otherwise Processed by GatherUp or its Sub-processors of which GatherUp becomes aware (a “Customer Data Incident”).
GatherUp shall make reasonable endeavors to identify the cause of such Customer Data Incident and take those steps as GatherUp deems necessary and reasonable in order to remediate the cause of such a Customer Data Incident to the extent the remediation is within GatherUp’s reasonable control. The obligations herein shall not apply to incidents that are caused by Customer or Customer’s Users.
7) Information collected by Account Owners and Users. Account owners and Users can store data that may contain Personal information in “Customer Notes”, “JobID”, “ExtraField” and “CustomField”. GatherUp has no direct relationship with the individuals whose Personal Data it hosts as part of those entry fields. Each Account owner is responsible for providing notice to its customers and third persons concerning the purpose for which the Personal Data is stored and how this Personal Data is processed.
8) Information collected by GatherUp. GatherUp collects the name, email address, mailing address, mobile phone number, and credit card information upon signup. GatherUp uses this information for administrative purposes and billing. GatherUp may also use the information to understand and analyze usage and preferences in order to improve the product and functionality. Data is only used in anonymized or aggregated form.
9) In compliance with GDPR Article 37 GatherUp has a designated DPO available for inquiries from data subjects on issues relating to data protection practices, withdrawal of consent, the right to be forgotten, and related rights. Please contact dpo@gatherup.com. Please also visit our GDPR help guide .
